title: Multi-device support
description: Service currently connects to one hardcoded MAC. Need BLE scan endpoint to discover all CoolLEDUX devices, device registry (MAC -> Controller map), per-device REST endpoints (e.g. /device/{mac}/power), and per-device MQTT topics.

title: Discover device-info toggle semantics (0x1E)
description:
Probe setDeviceInfo(int mode, boolean flag) at CoolledUXUtils.java:4843 on real hardware. APK comments are unhelpful; mode IDs known so far:
- 1 = 'config'
- 2 = 'brightness_auto' (ambient light sensor driven brightness)
- 3 = 'other_setting'

For each (mode, flag) pair: send the command, observe panel behavior, check whether state persists across reboot, and check whether the device emits a status frame we should parse. For mode 2 specifically: cover the LED with a hand vs bright light and watch brightness output. Document which modes are safe to expose as HA switches and which need more work.

Deliverable: short spec table + recommendation on which toggles to ship in the implementation task.
notes: Likely candidates map to toggles in SettingsCoolleduxFragment - worth grepping that fragment for which setDeviceInfo calls are actually wired to UI checkboxes. Skip modes the UI doesn't expose.
close_reason:
Reverse-engineered 0x1E device-info toggles from APK + hardware-verified on 16x96 (2026-04-16).

APK findings:
- CoolledUXUtils.java:4843 setDeviceInfo(action, on): [0x1E, subtype, 0|1] stream-framed, no CRC.
- Subtypes wired in SettingsCoolleduxFragment.java:
  - 0x01 = show_device_id_cb (DeviceManager.isShowDeviceId)
  - 0x02 = remote_cb (DeviceManager.isRemoteEnable)
  - 0x03 = iLedClock product line only, don't send on CoolLEDUX.
- Device emits response frame with type 0x1E (shape [0x1E, some_byte] per DeviceManager.java:4418).

Hardware validation:
- Both 0x01 and 0x02 subtypes accepted. State round-trips freely in both directions (observed true->false->true on both fields via /device/info).
- No visible panel change while a program is active — likely affects only the default/idle scroll.
- Bug discovered: the 0x1E response frame leaks into the same notification pipe as 0x1F. Our GetDeviceInfo parser rejects anything that isn't 0x1F, so a stale 0x1E ACK from a prior toggle causes an unrelated /device/info call to return 'not a device info response: type 0x1E'. Implementation bead 5i7 needs to filter/tolerate 0x1E in the device-info path.

Code artifacts kept from the probe (they're the 5i7 deliverable):
- CMD_SET_DEVICE_INFO, DEVICE_INFO_SUBTYPE_SHOW_ID, DEVICE_INFO_SUBTYPE_REMOTE constants.
- protocol.BuildSetDeviceInfoCommand builder.
- controller.SetShowDeviceID and controller.SetRemoteEnabled.

Debug endpoint /debug/device-toggle reverted.

Doc: docs/specs/protocol-ble.md gains a 'Device Info Toggles' section + catalog row updated to 'verified'.

title: Implement device-info toggles (0x1E)
description:
Ship switches for whichever 0x1E modes the discovery task validates as working.

Scope (conditional on discovery outcome):
- internal/protocol/commands.go: BuildDeviceInfoCommand(mode uint8, enabled bool).
- internal/controller/controller.go: SetAutoBrightness(ctx, bool), and any other toggles discovery says are safe.
- internal/api/handlers.go: POST /device-info/{mode} {enabled} or per-feature endpoints (POST /auto-brightness).
- internal/mqtt: one HA 'switch' entity per validated toggle.
- Tests.
- Update docs/specs/protocol-ble.md with only the modes we verified; mark unverified modes explicitly.

Do NOT ship a toggle for a mode the discovery task couldn't validate.
notes: Blocks on the discovery task. If discovery only validates auto-brightness, ship just that one switch and leave a TODO for the others. Don't guess.
close_reason:
Shipped 0x1E device-info toggles end-to-end (2026-04-16).

BUILDERS + CONTROLLER (landed in 59a commit):
- BuildSetDeviceInfoCommand(subtype, on) at internal/protocol/commands.go.
- SetShowDeviceID / SetRemoteEnabled via shared setDeviceInfoFlag helper at internal/controller/controller.go.
- setDeviceInfoFlag uses SendAndWait with RESPONSE_TYPE_SET_DEVICE_INFO (0x1E) to DRAIN the ACK — that was the bug discovered in 59a where stale 0x1E frames leaked into GetDeviceInfo calls.

REST:
- POST /device/show-id {on: bool} -> h.SetShowDeviceID
- POST /device/remote {on: bool} -> h.SetRemote
- shared handleDeviceInfoToggle helper for the common body-parse + setter dispatch.

MQTT:
- SwitchConfig entity struct.
- BuildShowDeviceIDSwitchConfig + BuildRemoteEnableSwitchConfig discovery builders via shared buildDeviceInfoSwitch helper.
- HandleShowDeviceIDCommand + HandleRemoteCommand via shared handleSwitchToggle helper; parses HA-style ON/OFF.
- Both entities published in publishDiscovery; both topics subscribed in subscribeTopics.

TESTS (6 new, all green):
- protocol/commands_test: TestBuildSetDeviceInfoCommand with 4 subcases covering both subtypes x both states.
- controller/controller_test: 4 tests covering ACK consume (both fields), explicit OFF case, and rejected-response-type guard.
- api/server_test: disconnected round-trip for both endpoints, plus InvalidBody.
- mqtt/handlers_test: connected ON/OFF for both handlers, whitespace/case tolerance, bad-payload rejection.

HARDWARE VALIDATION (2026-04-16, v10 firmware):
- Previously flaky parser interference is gone. Each POST + immediate GET /device/info now round-trips cleanly: show_id true->false->true, remote true->false->true all confirmed in a single command stream with no 'type 0x1E' errors.
- Both toggles affect only the default/idle scroll, not active programs — consistent with 59a finding.

DOCS:
- docs/specs/protocol-rest.md: new /device/show-id and /device/remote sections.
- docs/specs/protocol-mqtt.md: new topic listings, switch entity descriptions, command payload example.

title: Stopwatch overlay rendering (match countdown)
description: REST endpoint /stopwatch and BLE command 0x10 are wired, but stopwatch never got the composite-program treatment countdown has: no APK-matched hourglass bitmap, no composite 0x03+0x0a wrapping. Mirror the countdown approach (timecount.go) using the APK's stopwatch assets to render a usable visual on 16x96.

comments.author: Loren Lisk
comments.text: APK research complete. 16x96 stopwatch time-count layout is byte-identical to countdown's; only differences are the background animation GIF (ic_stopwatch_bg_animation_1696.gif, 2157 B) and the control command family (0x10 vs 0x0F). Implemented: asset extraction hook in scripts/extract-assets.sh, buildStopwatchProgram96x16 in timecount.go, Controller.StopwatchDisplay, 'show' action in /stopwatch handler, REST spec update, 13 new tests (all pass). Still needs hardware verification on the physical panel before closing.

title: Scoreboard rendering investigation (0x11 on 16x96)
description: Scoreboard command 0x11 is ACKed by this firmware but produces no visible output on the 16x96 panel (REST spec already documents this). Investigate whether it's fundamentally unsupported on this SKU or whether a composite-program path could make it render. Likely closes as 'wontfix' if firmware just drops it.
close_reason: Shipped and hardware-verified: composite 0x0B content block, SetScores now takes 4 args (including period counters), documented the SetTime-while-running firmware quirk.

title: Raw-GIF content type 0x0C (firmware v30+)
description: Firmware v30+ supports uploading a raw GIF via content type 0x0C, letting the device decode it directly. Lower bandwidth than our current frame-by-frame 0x03 path, but 0x03 works fine on this device, so this is non-urgent. Revisit if we need faster GIF uploads or want to match APK behavior more closely.
notes:
APK discovery complete (2026-04-15). See memory/project_raw_gif_0x0c.md.

Builders: CoolledUXUtils.java:3103-3230 (4 overloads: resource, file path, object wrapper, encrypted).

Inner payload byte layout:
  0x0C, 0x00*7, layerType(1B=0x01), 0x00, startCol(2BE), startRow(2BE),
  width(2BE), height(2BE), gifLen(4BE), rawGifBytes
Outer: [4BE length = innerLen+4][inner]

Transport identical to 0x03: WrapProgramPayload (8 zeros + count=1 + 0x00),
LZSS, 0x02 3-arg program start with CRC32. No new command codes.

Version gate (CoolledUXUtils.java:2826): version<30 || version>=255 => fall
back to 0x03, else 0x0C. Version source is BLE scan record byte 21
(DeviceManager.java:5633) -- not a command response. Capturing this
requires advertising data at scan time; our current BLE client discards it.

Encrypted variant (line 3202): only used for app-internal GIFs; first 32
bytes XOR 0xDA. Not needed for user GIF uploads.

Device-type gate (DeviceManager.java:4610): only applied when DEVICE_TYPE
in {37-45, 48, 49}. JT_HW358.02 16x96 likely qualifies but should be
confirmed before flipping.

Remaining work (not done here): (1) expose scan-record byte 21 through our
BLE client, (2) add a DeviceManager.CoolleduxGifAnimationProgramContent
equivalent and builder in internal/protocol/program.go, (3) route /gif to
0x0C when firmware>=30. Still P4 / non-urgent; 0x03 works fine today.
close_reason:
Implemented opt-in raw-GIF content type 0x0C with hardware validation (2026-04-15).

BUILDER: internal/protocol/program.go BuildRawGIFContent matches APK byte layout from CoolledUXUtils.java:3103-3200. Verified via TestBuildRawGIFContent (4 cases) and TestBuildRawGIFProgram.

API: /display/gif accepts raw:true flag. When set, GIF is uploaded verbatim via content type 0x0C; frame_duration and fit are ignored. Default remains the frame-by-frame 0x03 path.

HARDWARE TEST (v10 panel, expected negative):
  - Firmware version decoded from btmon scan-record byte 21 = 0x0A (10 decimal, v30+ required).
  - Baseline raw:false: 4 frames, 12330 bytes raw -> 1514 compressed, 2 chunks ACKed, panel cycled R/G/B/W as expected.
  - Raw raw:true: 405 bytes raw -> 165 compressed, 1 chunk. Program start ACKed, chunk 0 NOT ACKed (5s timeout). Panel reverted to default '1. CoolLED' rainbow scroll. Same firmware-fallback signature as every other ACK-but-misunderstood case (layer_type=0, LZSS disabled, etc.).

Byte layout confirmed correct (405 = 369 GIF + 26 content header + 10 wrapper). Positive render test impossible on v10 panel; revisit if v30+ hardware becomes available.

Docs updated: CLAUDE.md note 20, docs/specs/protocol-ble.md (0x0C section), docs/specs/protocol-rest.md (raw field).

description:
Expose the device-side orientation state machine.

Scope:

- internal/protocol/commands.go: BuildDriveStateSetCommand(state DriveState) and BuildDriveStateGetCommand().
- internal/protocol/response.go: parse the 0x1C response into the enum.
- internal/controller/controller.go: SetDriveState(ctx, state) / GetDriveState(ctx).
- internal/api/handlers.go: POST /drive-state {state}, GET /drive-state.

- Tests in protocol and controller packages.
- Update docs/specs/protocol-ble.md and docs/specs/protocol-rest.md and docs/specs/protocol-mqtt.md.
notes: Blocks on the drive-state discovery task. Don't collapse this into the flip/rotate (0x0C) command; they're separate code paths in the APK and may be additive on hardware.

This is for the iLedCar/iDevilEyes product line. No implementation to ship. If 23i (multi-device support) ever adds iLedCar, regenerate builders from the APK (CoolledUXUtils.java:4277 / :4419).

title: Implement color animation modes (0x13/0x02 + 0x13/0x03)
description:
Add color animation support beyond the current single-color 0x13/0x01. Wire builder, REST endpoint, and MQTT entity.

Scope:
- internal/protocol/commands.go: add BuildColorModeCommand(mode int, patternBytes []byte, params ...byte) and BuildColorSpeedCommand(speed uint8).
- internal/controller/controller.go: SetColorMode(ctx, modeID) and SetColorSpeed(ctx, speed).
- internal/api/handlers.go: POST /color/mode {mode, speed?} and POST /color/speed {speed}.
- internal/mqtt: HA discovery for a 'select' entity listing modes 1..31 and a 'number' entity for speed 1..10.
- Tests: table-driven in commands_test.go, controller_test.go covering each mode.
- Update docs/specs/protocol-ble.md with the 0x13/0x02 and 0x13/0x03 layouts.

Embedded patterns come from the discovery task output.
notes: Blocks on the discovery task. Keep the existing BuildColorCommand (0x13/0x01) untouched. Verify on hardware that each mode renders before closing.
close_reason:
Implemented color animation modes (0x13/0x02 + 0x13/0x03) end-to-end with hardware validation (2026-04-15).

BUILDERS (internal/protocol/colormode.go):
- BuildColorSpeedCommand(speed) — trivial [0x13][0x02][speed].
- BuildColorModeCommand(mode) — looks up the 29-entry table (1,2,5..31) and emits [0x13][0x03][i3][i4?][i2][palette]. i4 uses int8 with -1 sentinel because its presence vs absence changes animation family on the firmware.
- 12 tests including a byte-exact mode-13 fixture and a regression guard on mode-14 (smallest packet).

CONTROLLER (internal/controller/controller.go):
- SetColorSpeed(ctx, speed) and SetColorMode(ctx, mode), both with response-type check.

REST (internal/api/):
- POST /display/color/mode {mode}  → 400 for unsupported modes, 500 for transport
- POST /display/color/speed {speed}

MQTT (internal/mqtt/):
- SelectConfig + NumberConfig entity structs; BuildColorModeSelectConfig publishes a HA select with options ['off', '1', '2', '5', ...]; BuildColorSpeedNumberConfig publishes a slider (1-10). HandleColorModeCommand/HandleColorSpeedCommand wired as plain-text topic handlers.

HARDWARE VALIDATION (16x96 v10 firmware, 01:00:00:FB:A4:16):
- Modes 1,2,5,6,7,8,11,12,13,14,19,20,31 probed one-at-a-time with user visual feedback.
- i4 meaning pinned down: 0=scroll R→L, 1=scroll L→R, 2=scroll B→T, 3=scroll T→B, 4=converge, 5=diverge.
- i2 = palette position count (byte count / 2), confirmed.
- i3 = transition style: i3=1+no-i4 = temporal pulse w/ black gaps; i3=4+no-i4 = continuous crossfade; i3=2,3+i4 = spatial scroll (i3=2 vs i3=3 couldn't be cleanly isolated because every i3=3 mode in the APK also has a different i4).
- Mode 3 correctly rejected with HTTP 400.
- Speed scaling confirmed (speed=1 visibly slower than speed=10 on mode 1).

DOCS:
- docs/specs/protocol-ble.md: replaced 'Probe plan' section with 'Validated semantics' + 'Remaining unknowns'. Catalog entries marked verified.
- docs/specs/protocol-rest.md: new /display/color/mode and /display/color/speed sections.
- docs/specs/protocol-mqtt.md: new topic listings, select + number entity descriptions, command payload examples.
- CLAUDE.md note 21 added.

Full test suite green.

title: Discover drive-state orientation semantics (0x1C/0x01, 0x1C/0x02)
description:
Verify on-hardware behavior of setDriveState(int) and getDriveState() from CoolledUXUtils.java:4277. Document what each state code actually does on a 16x96 panel:
- 0 NORMAL, 1 LEFT, 2 RIGHT, 3 BACK, 4 PARK, 5 EMERGENCY

For each state, capture: any on-device rotation/mirror applied to already-uploaded content, whether it persists across power cycle, whether it interacts with the existing 0x0C flip/mirror command, and what getDriveState's response payload looks like (response parser in DeviceManager.java).

Produce a short spec suitable for dropping into docs/specs/protocol-ble.md and a decision on whether EMERGENCY does something visually distinct (flashing? red? UI fragment hint).
notes: Reference Java: CoolledUXUtils.java:4277 (getDriveState), search for 'setDriveState' and 'DriveState' in DeviceManager.java and light/coolledux/ UI fragments (ILedCarDriveFragment) for semantics.
close_reason:
Reverse-engineered 0x1C drive-state from APK + hardware-verified not supported on 16x96 (2026-04-16).

APK findings (CoolledUXUtils.java:4277 get, :4419 set; ILedCarDriveFragment.java:25-30 for state codes):
- 0x1C/0x01 set: [0x1C, 0x01, state] stream-framed, no CRC. States 0=NORMAL, 1=LEFT, 2=RIGHT, 3=BACK, 4=PARK, 5=EMERGENCY.
- 0x1C/0x02 get: [0x1C, 0x02]. Response parsed at DeviceManager.java:3620 as [0x1C, state_byte].
- UI is shipped for the iLedCar/iDevilEyes product line (car-mounted signs). The CoolLEDUX 16x96 shares BLE service UUIDs but not the overlay.

Hardware validation (2026-04-16, JT_HW358.02 v10, 01:00:00:FB:A4:16):
- get 0x1C/0x02 -> 5s timeout, no response bytes.
- set for states 0, 1, 5 -> no visible effect on a panel showing static text.

Confirms the existing catalog note 'no response on this device'.

No shippable code. Spec updated at docs/specs/protocol-ble.md with a dedicated 'Drive State' section and catalog rows now marked 'not supported on 16x96'. Per feedback memory, the temporary debug endpoint and builder code were fully reverted; regenerate from the APK if 23i ever adds iLedCar support.

title: Password commands (0x0D/0x0E)
description: Android app uses XOR-encoded password commands (0x0D to set, 0x0E to verify). Protocol is documented in the APK decompilation but has not been tested on hardware. Implement command builders, response parsing, and a REST endpoint; verify against a device.

title: Discover color-mode/speed byte layout (0x13/0x02, 0x13/0x03)
description: Reverse-engineer the exact packet layout for setColorMode(int) and setColorSpeed(int) from CoolledUXUtils.java (lines 4714 and 4835). Extract all 31+ mode hex-pattern strings (colorMode10, colorMode14, colorMode19..., plus inline literals). For each mode, document: mode ID, pattern bytes, default duration/repeat params (i2, i3, i4, i5 in the switch). Produce a table (mode -> pattern hex + trailing params) and a probe plan for verifying on real hardware. No code changes in this task.
notes: Reference: references/apk-decompiled/light/utils/CoolledUXUtils.java. Also grep for 'colorMode' static field declarations earlier in the file for the large embedded patterns. Output format: markdown table committed under docs/specs/ or attached as bd notes.
close_reason:
Reverse-engineered 0x13/0x02 and 0x13/0x03 from the APK. Spec committed to docs/specs/protocol-ble.md 'Color Mode and Speed' section.

Key findings:
- 0x13/0x02 is trivial: [speed:1].
- 0x13/0x03 structure: [i3][i4 if >=0][i2][palette]; i4 is conditionally present.
- All 31 mode rows confirmed from smali (CoolledUXUtils.smali:20288). jadx couldn't cleanly reconstruct the control flow; register reuse put str2-assignments on the wrong branches. Trust smali.
- Palette aliasing: colorMode1==2==4==5==6 (180B); colorMode9 aliases 11,12,15,16; colorMode17==18; colorMode13==31.
- Modes 3 and 4 fall through every branch to an empty no-op default. Don't expose them.
- colorMode21 has a trailing comma in the APK source (harmless but noted).

Probe plan (7 cases) documented in the spec so o2l has a clean validation sequence.

Research-only; no code changes. Implementation blocked bead: o2l.
